corpora.nativeSidecarWrites: Two disposable 2k-tree images received stars/flags and two-step Undo; two matching XMP files remain. No 10k-tree or flat source decisions were edited.

notes: Recording finalized successfully, but export contained no time-profile rows. Analyzer rejected it. Do not interpret this as zero CPU work or stalls. No raw trace/XML is committed.

checks: Scrolls down and back during EXIF indexing
Keyboard next photo and Z to genuine JPEG 100%, then Fit/contact sheet
Direct parent starts empty; Include Subfolders shows 2000
Two-card group stars and flags leave other cards unchanged; two-step Undo
Day parent shows 1000; card child 250; scope follows sidebar navigation
Direct mode retains focused child photo
Two-image/two-sidecar Trash confirmation uses relative names; cancelled without native moves
Existing single-folder stress corpus responds to scrolling during EXIF indexing

notes: One-second process RSS/ps CPU samples during scripted native indexing and input; automation overhead included. RSS is not a whole-session peak or physical footprint. ps CPU is a process statistic, not sampled main-thread work, frame time or instantaneous utilization.
Native Photo RSS sampled using ps about once per second during recording AND finalization; profiling/automation overhead included. This is not a whole-session peak or physical footprint.

Final service cases run sequentially tree2k, tree10k, tree10k, tree2k, flat10k in fresh processes with temporary FULL-durability SQLite. No overlapping build/test/native input during timing. Earlier exploratory runs remain private.

Byte hashing warms filesystem caches; repeated three-template gradients lack real RAW/EXIF diversity. The distributed tree uses ASCII frame names; the retained flat corpus has accented names. These differing inventories are not a matched before/after trial and selection timing differences are not credited to the UI-region change.

Native checks ran in a 1280x820-point Retina window, Contact Sheet size160/filmstrip120, Filename/All flags/All stars, grouping/auto-advance off and no EXIF labels. Native inputs are scripted; no FPS, physical-trackpad, real-card, concurrent-copy or 40k acceptance claim.

Native 2k memory covers a short attempted profile plus finalization with Preview initially visible. Native 10k memory covers a 30-second indexing/contact-sheet input window. Different scenarios/windows and profiling overhead prevent a matched memory comparison.

Personal decisions and file-operation jobs were not initiated. The original three-photo Preview/settings were restored and only the three temporary sidebar shortcuts removed. Corpus images and raw artifacts stay outside Git.
Fresh process recommended per run; temporary SQLite database, unchanged FULL durability, no image/sidecar writes or shared thumbnail disk cache.
All input image bytes hashed before/after outside timing/sampling. OS caches are warmed by hashing; cold means new process/database, not cold physical storage.
IncludesSubfolders identifies combined parent-folder scope; distinct same-named files retain their folder identities. File-count ceiling includes all descendants.
Folder-open repeats inventory after validation/hashing. Timings include actual workspace model and per-photo display records.
First Fit and selected readiness overlap full EXIF/decision indexing; readiness polls at 1ms, not native keyboard-to-display time.
Navigation uses model selection and the Fit pipeline at 2560px, with a 64MiB RAM cache. Forward/reverse/spread do not guarantee cache hits; decode counts are reported.
No SwiftUI rendering, thumbnail-grid loading, 35ms view debounce, presented frames, full RAW detail or bulk save/XMP throughput in this service report.

Preflight inventory/byte hashing runs before the first RSS checkpoint; its retained input URLs coexist with the workspace inventory. Baseline/helper allocations are included, so service RSS is not native Photo RSS.
Process RSS sampled about every 10ms plus phase checkpoints; includes runtime/allocator/decoder/model memory, not a whole-app peak bound. The heartbeat is not frame time.
